# Lumper (01, engineer) — BAD-009

## Brief
Add a smoke job to BadTakes CI that boots the Electron app headless on every PR and push to main, starting with SMOKE_SCOPE=home against a temp copy of the committed fixture library (TODO.md item 40). No CI job has ever booted the app.

Setup: you are in the worktree .claude/worktrees/bad-009-smoke-ci on branch chore/bad-009-smoke-ci. Run `bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` first. Follow the repo's CLAUDE.md and .claude/skills/implementing-changes (what proves a change).

Shape: a new job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (keep the file's comment style: say why, not what). Linux ubuntu-latest under xvfb-run is the expected route; windows-latest is the fallback if Linux cannot be made reliable. Recipe: npm ci; cp -R fixtures/library to a temp dir and point BT_LIBRARY_ROOT at the copy (never the committed tree: the home leg installs a zip into it); SMOKE_SCOPE=home; SMOKE_DIR to a temp dir; the step trusts the exit code (SMOKE_FAIL exits non-zero); upload SMOKE_DIR screenshots with actions/upload-artifact on failure (match the action major versions ci.yml already pins). Read .github/workflows/gate.yml and decide whether the new job must be wired into Gate so it actually blocks a merge; do so if Gate aggregates the other ci.yml jobs.

Known Linux traps to handle deliberately, not by trial: Ubuntu 24.04 runners restrict unprivileged user namespaces through AppArmor, so Electron's sandbox can abort at launch (prefer fixing it in the job, e.g. sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0, over weakening the sandbox in main.js); xvfb-run needs a screen size; dbus noise on stderr is harmless. Any main.js change must be scoped to --smoke and justified in a comment. ffmpeg is not needed for the home leg; leave the wider legs (tableread onward, screening needs ffmpeg) to a later change, but state in a ci.yml comment how to widen. docs/superpowers/research/2026-09-12-desktop-smoke-surface.md (merged in #327) measured the walkthrough; read its findings on the home leg's cost.

Local proof: SMOKE_SCOPE=home with BT_LIBRARY_ROOT at a temp copy prints SMOKE_OK and exits 0 on this Mac, and the fixtures/library tree is untouched afterward. If you can reproduce the Linux job in a podman ubuntu:24.04 container with xvfb in reasonable time (containers are podman, never Docker or OrbStack), do it and report the result; if not, say so and Spud will iterate on CI. Do not push, commit, or open the PR: Spud does that and watches the run.

Docs: update the CLAUDE.md smoke bullet and implementing-changes SKILL.md only where they now state something false (for example that no CI job runs smoke), and mark TODO.md item 40 done or narrowed per that file's convention.

## Ticket proposals
- **Make the CI smoke job a required check once it has run green** — suggested P2; created as [[BAD-022]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: Branch protection on BadTakes main requires only the Gate check, so the new ci.yml smoke job (BAD-009) reports a red run on a PR without blocking the merge; Spud's landing waits only for required checks, so a broken app boot would still land. ci.yml is path-filtered, which is why Gate exists: requiring smoke directly would strand docs-only PRs, so the change needs either a required check that tolerates a skipped job or a Gate that needs smoke.
  Evidence: gh api repos/0snug0/BadTakes/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks -> contexts: [Gate]; gate.yml has no needs: and its header explains why filtered checks cannot be required.
